Dear Mercer,

We have received a maintenance report from the tenant regarding the washing machine at the property.

The tenant has advised that the Harbour Surveying washing machine is not heating the water during wash cycles set to 60°C or higher. As a result, they are unable to properly wash clothing that requires higher-temperature cycles in accordance with the garment care instructions.

I have attached the photograph supplied by the tenant for your reference.

Please let me know if you would be happy for me to arrange for our appliance engineer to attend and investigate the fault.

Kind regards,

input.context: Landlord approved engineer attendance (no amount). No completion report on file; on 27 Feb contractor (Harper) called tenant asking to schedule visit.

input.situation_text: Contractor sent invoice £75.11 with no completion report; the day before, contractor still calling tenant to schedule visit. Landlord approved attendance with no cost cap. Invoice document not attached.

lessons.situation: A confirmed repair visit has taken place, but the agency has received no work results or completion report from the contractor, so the operator has to find out what happened.
lessons.action: Phone the maintenance provider directly to ask for the job status instead of waiting for a written update. Confirm the work was completed, how any new keys will be handed over, and how the invoice will be sent, reminding them to quote the job ID in email replies. Then move the task to Result, mark the request completed, and start the final checks.
lessons.rationale: A direct call settles the missing completion information quickly and also sets out the invoicing and key-handover steps needed to close the job cleanly.

lessons.situation: A repair visit has been confirmed with both the tenant and the contractor, the appointment time has passed, and no completion report or work results have come back.
lessons.action: Do not close the job or assume the works were done. Place the job on hold as 'waiting on response' and chase the contractor for an outcome of the visit (attended or not, work done, follow-up needed). Check with the tenant if the contractor stays silent, and review the job again once a reply arrives.
lessons.rationale: Without a completion report from the contractor, the real status of the visit is unknown, so the job must stay open and be actively followed up rather than progressed or closed.

lessons.situation: A contractor attended a scheduled repair visit, but the system showed no work results afterwards and flagged the job for checking; the contractor's invoice note then described the fault found, the fix and a successful test.
lessons.action: When no work results have been logged after a completed visit, check the contractor's invoice note for the findings and outcome, and treat it as the completion record if it confirms the fault, the fix and a passing test. Move the task to Result, mark the request completed and start the final checks. Skip optional document uploads that aren't needed, recording the reason. Then request the landlord's confirmation before closing.
lessons.rationale: The invoice note can serve as proof of completion when no separate report exists, and the landlord should still confirm before the job is closed.

lessons.situation: A confirmed repair visit has passed (a second attempt after an earlier failed fix) and the system has flagged that no work results or completion update have been received from the contractor.
lessons.action: Review the case thread to see whether the contractor has sent any message that still needs a reply from the agency. If nothing is outstanding, return the request to auto mode so the standard chasers for completion or results continue, and do not escalate or re-book manually.
lessons.rationale: A missing work result often just means the contractor's update has not arrived yet, so the first step is to confirm whether the ball is in the agency's court before intervening, and otherwise let automation resume the follow-up.

lessons.situation: A contractor who completed an approved cleaning job emails to say their invoice has been sent to the agency's operator, while the request is on hold waiting for the provider and the system is prompting the operator to check whether a reply is needed or to return the request to auto mode.
lessons.action: When the contractor confirms the invoice has been sent, no reply to them is needed. Move the task to the result/completed state, mark the request as completed for final checks, and forward the invoice to the landlord with a short covering note. Record that landlord confirmation is needed, then close the request once the final checks are done.
lessons.rationale: A contractor's invoice notification is an informational closing message rather than a question, so the right response is to progress closeout and pass the invoice to the landlord instead of replying or leaving the request on hold.

input.subject: Washing machine repair – Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane, Cedarford ZZ9 0ZZ – Ref R/PM042-2 (NBL-042) – invoice £75.11
input.body:
Dear Lantern Services,

Thank you for your email regarding invoice for GBP 75.11 for the washing machine repair at Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane, Cedarford, ZZ9 0ZZ (ref R/PM042-2 / NBL-042).

Before we can pass this to the landlord, we need the outcome of the visit. We have no completion report on file, and our records show a call on 27 February from your engineer asking the tenant to arrange a visit, so we are unclear whether the job has been attended yet.

Please could you reply confirming:
1. The date the engineer attended the property.
2. What fault was found and what work was carried out (e.g. heating element/thermostat replaced), and whether the machine now heats correctly on 60°C cycles.
3. Whether any further work or parts are needed.

Please also attach the invoice itself (PDF) quoting the job reference and property address, as we cannot currently see the invoice document on the job.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

input.body:
Dear Noah,

We are following up on the washing machine repair at Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane, Cedarford, ZZ9 0ZZ (ref R/PM042-2 / NBL-042).

Could you let us know whether the engineer from Lantern Services has visited yet and, if so, whether the washing machine is now heating properly on 60°C cycles? If they haven't attended, please tell us whether a visit has been arranged and when.

We have also asked Lantern Services for an update and will be back in touch by 1 March.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

data.reasoning:
There's no evidence the work was actually done, and the timeline looks inconsistent—the visit date even precedes the scheduling call. The invoice has no visible amount, the approval lacks a figure, and the due date looks off. I should message the contractor directly to confirm whether the visit happened and chase the outcome before forwarding anything.

Following the lesson to check with the tenant if the contractor stays quiet, I'll also ask the tenant to confirm whether the engineer showed up, since that runs in parallel and helps resolve the conflict. I'll send the landlord a brief note too, since the job is on hold due to the invoice issue and they should stay informed—keeping it proportionate to just these three messages. I'll also flag the duplicate ticket as a risk without escalating, and place a short hold while things get sorted.

result.summary: Lantern Services has sent a £75.11 invoice (event 024), but nothing on file shows the work was done. The day before, on 27 Feb, the contractor (Harper) was still calling the tenant to arrange a visit (event 022). The invoice document isn't on the job either. So I haven't forwarded it to the landlord or moved the job to close-out. I've asked Lantern Services what happened at the visit and for the invoice PDF, asked the tenant whether the engineer has been, and put the job on hold with a follow-up in 2 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord approved an engineer visit with no cost cap (event 008, approval 55, no amount). An invoice can only go to the landlord once the work is confirmed. Here the records point the other way: the visit slot of 23/02 15:25 (event 017) is earlier than the scheduling calls that evening (events 015–016). On 26 Feb the system flagged that no work results had come back (event 020). On 27 Feb the contractor was still asking to schedule (event 022). Following lessons #19 and #32, I'm not assuming the work was done and am chasing the contractor for the outcome. Lesson #18 (treating the invoice note as the completion record) doesn't fit, because the invoice email describes no findings, fix or test. Lesson #3 (forward the invoice and close) assumes the job is complete, which isn't confirmed here.
